title: Internal and sectionwise module operations agree
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For each scheme $T$ use the small pro-étale site with its universe convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the sheafified tensor product of abelian sheaves [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], the pulled-back ring object $\Lambda_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and its reconstructed section-ring sheaf $B_T$. Let
$$E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathrm{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(B_T)$$
be the canonical equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Write $f^*_{\rm int},f_{*,\rm int}$ for the internal module functors and their specified adjunction [def-sfb-module-upper-star], [def-sfb-module-lower-star], [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. For $f:T'\to T$ let $f^*_{\rm sec},f_{*,\rm sec}$ be the sectionwise ringed-topos functors for the ring isomorphism $f^{-1}B_T\cong B_{T'}$ induced by $\alpha_f$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]: pullback is $B_{T'}\otimes_{f^{-1}B_T}f^{-1}(-)$ (sheafified sectionwise tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), and direct image is ordinary sheaf direct image with scalar restriction along the adjunct $B_T\to f_*B_{T'}$, with their canonical adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Then the canonical comparisons give
$$E_{T'}f^*_{\rm int}\cong f^*_{\rm sec}E_T,\qquad E_Tf_{*,\rm int}\cong f_{*,\rm sec}E_{T'},$$
and identify the specified internal adjunction with the sectionwise ringed-topos adjunction, including its unit and counit. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, write $j_{!,\rm int}$ for [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and $j_{!,\rm sec}$ for the sectionwise extension by zero, the left adjoint to $j^*_{\rm sec}$. There is a canonical comparison
$$E_Tj_{!,\rm int}\cong j_{!,\rm sec}E_U$$
identifying these open adjunctions. In a cartesian square of schemes with open vertical immersions and compatible pulled-back coefficients, these comparisons identify the internal open-extension base-change transformation with the sectionwise one (the transformation defined as the adjunction mate of the pullback-composition comparison). Thus whenever that sectionwise transformation is invertible, so is the internal one. The equivalences $E_T$ are additive exact equivalences, so exactness and exact sequences of these operations transport between the two module categories.

source.place: Step 1, hidden identification of internal and sectionwise module operations, and Step 2, identification of their canonical base-change maps; compare Stacks sites-modules.tex Tags 03D6 (definition-pushforward) and 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules).

proof.text: Fix $f:T'\to T$ and abbreviate the two internal module categories by $\mathcal I_T,\mathcal I_{T'}$ and the sectionwise categories by $\mathcal S_T,\mathcal S_{T'}$. The equivalence $E_T$ leaves underlying abelian sheaves, section groups and restriction maps unchanged by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. In particular it sends an action $a:\Lambda_T\otimes M\to M$ to $r\cdot m=a(r\otimes m)$ on each object of the site. Its action on morphisms is the same underlying sheaf map, so it preserves sums of morphisms and zero morphisms. The same holds for a quasi-inverse: internal action maps are reconstructed uniquely from these sectionwise bilinear maps using the sheafified tensor product [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure]. Thus the equivalences and their quasi-inverses are additive.

source.place: Tags 03D6 (definition-pushforward), 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules); the internal comparison is the agent argument here.

proof.text:
Write $V'=V\times_TT'$ for a pro-étale object $V\to T$. By [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] both direct images have underlying sections $N(V')$. For the canonical lax tensor structure of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-lax-monoidal], its map on pure section tensors is $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$ evaluated on $V'$: indeed this bilinear presheaf map followed by the tensor-sheafification unit induces the structure map, uniquely by [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure]. Consequently the action formula of [def-sfb-module-lower-star] sends $(r,n)$ to $\eta_f(r)\cdot n$ in $N(V')$. By [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], $\eta_f=f_*\alpha_f\circ\eta^{\rm Ab}_f$, exactly the adjunct used for the sectionwise scalar restriction. Hence the identity of the underlying direct-image sheaf is a linear isomorphism
$$r_f:E_T f_{*,\rm int}\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{*,\rm sec}E_{T'}.$$
It commutes with restrictions and with morphisms of $N$ because all three maps in the action formula do. This proves naturality, not just an objectwise identification.

source.place: Tags 03D6 (definition-pushforward), 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules); the internal comparison is the agent argument here.

proof.text:
Conjugate the specified internal adjunction by $E_T,E_{T'}$, writing $A=E_{T'} f^*_{\rm int}E_T^{-1}$ and $B=E_T f_{*,\rm int}E_{T'}^{-1}$. Its Hom bijection is obtained from [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] by the fully faithful Hom identifications of the equivalences. Put $L=f^*_{\rm sec}$ and $R=f_{*,\rm sec}$; the sectionwise adjunction $L\dashv R$ is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], with the same coefficient map as in Step 2. Step 2 gives $r:B\cong R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to $A\dashv B$, $L\dashv R$, and $\delta=r^{-1}$. It gives the unique natural isomorphism $c:A\cong L$ satisfying
$$B(c_M)\eta^A_M=r^{-1}_{LM}\eta^L_M.$$
Undoing the conjugation gives $c_f:E_{T'}f^*_{\rm int}\cong f^*_{\rm sec}E_T$. All Hom sets lie in the common containing universe from the stated site convention; no large-index colimit is used.

source.place: Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints), adjunction Hom characterization and its unit/counit equations.

proof.text:
The comparison in Step 3 is canonical relative to the specified adjunctions: it is the unique isomorphism with the displayed unit normalization. Here $A$ uses precisely the extension-of-scalars pullback of [def-sfb-module-upper-star] and the specified composite adjunction of [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]; $L$ uses precisely the sheafified tensor-formula pullback and canonical Hom bijection stated in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Write these two natural Hom bijections as $\Phi_A,\Phi_L$. Naturality in the target and the unit equation of Step 3 give, for every $h:LM\to N$,
$$\Phi_L(h)=r_N\,\Phi_A(hc_M).$$
Indeed the right side is $r_N B(h)B(c_M)\eta^A_M=R(h)r_{LM}r^{-1}_{LM}\eta^L_M=R(h)\eta^L_M$. Taking $h=\mathrm{id}_{LM}$ recovers the unit equation. Taking $h=\varepsilon^L_N\circ L(r_N)$ and $M=BN$ gives
$$\varepsilon^A_N=\varepsilon^L_N\circ L(r_N)\circ c_{BN},$$
since both sides transpose to $\mathrm{id}_{BN}$. The formulas for transposition, units and counits are exactly [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Thus the actual Hom bijections, units and counits agree under $c,r$, rather than merely the isomorphism classes of the functors.

source.place: Tags 03D6 (definition-pushforward), 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules); the internal comparison is the agent argument here.

proof.text:
For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] supplies the internal adjunction $j_{!,\rm int}\dashv j^*_{\rm int}$; its underlying left functor is abelian extension by zero with the displayed linearized action. Conjugate this adjunction by $E_U,E_T$. Its right adjoint is identified with $j^*_{\rm sec}$ by $c_j$ from Steps 3–4. The sectionwise $j_{!,\rm sec}$ in the statement is equipped with its extension-by-zero adjunction to that same right adjoint. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] again, now to these two left adjoints of the identified restriction functor. This gives
$$o_j:E_Tj_{!,\rm int}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,\rm sec}E_U,$$
uniquely normalized by the units. Its Hom characterization is exactly the one in Step 4 with $j_!$ in place of $f^*$ and $j^*$ in place of $f_*$. Evaluating on identity maps, using [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], identifies the counits as well. This argument uses the variable ring-sheaf adjunction in the statement; it does not apply a constant-finite-coefficient extension-by-zero lemma to $B_T$.

source.place: Linear extension by zero and Extension by zero clauses; comparison by the unit-normalized adjoint uniqueness argument of Step 3.

proof.text: For composable $T''\xrightarrow fT'\xrightarrow gT$, the isomorphism of direct images in [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp] is the underlying sheaf composition isomorphism. Evaluating it on $V$ merely rebrackets $(V\times_TT')\times_{T'}T''\cong V\times_TT''$. Since $r_f,r_g,r_{gf}$ are identities on these section groups with the same scalar restrictions, their square with this composition isomorphism commutes. The specified pullback-composition isomorphism [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] is its conjugate under the composite adjunction. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], this conjugation is a bijection characterized by the unit/counit formula. Steps 3–4 identify those units and counits. Thus both routes through the square comparing internal and sectionwise pullback compositions have the same conjugate, namely the just-compared direct-image composition, and are equal by injectivity of that bijection. The same reasoning compares the two composites attached to the equal scheme morphisms in a commutative square.

source.place: Definition of the composition comparison as conjugate to direct-image composition.

proof.text:
Write the cartesian open square as $j':U'\hookrightarrow T'$, $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, $g:T'\to T$, $g':U'\to U$, with $gj'=jg'$. Let
$$b:g'^*j^*\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^*g^*$$
be the comparison through pullback along that equal composite. In the convention of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], its inverse-transpose (left mate) is the following completely specified open-extension transformation:
$$\beta:j'_!g'^*\xrightarrow{j'_!g'^*\eta_j}j'_!g'^*j^*j_!\xrightarrow{j'_!b j_!}j'_!j'^*g^*j_!\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{j'}g^*j_!}g^*j_!.$$
Step 6 identifies $b$; Step 5 identifies $\eta_j,\varepsilon_{j'}$; and Steps 3 and 5 identify all intervening functors. Applying the equivalences to this displayed composite therefore gives exactly the sectionwise composite with these same three factors. This proves equality of the canonical mate transformations. In the convention that writes the invertible open-extension comparison in the reverse direction, the comparison of inverses follows by composing the obtained equality with the two inverses. No pro-étale stalk-conservativity claim or independent base-change theorem is being used.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), adjunction definition of the exchange map; the left-mate formula is the inverse formula in def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate.

proof.text: The sectionwise category is abelian by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], since the sites have the stated size convention. For each $T$, apply [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits] to $E_T$ and its quasi-inverse. Both preserve zero objects, kernels and cokernels. Their additivity was proved in Step 1, so both are exact: a sequence is exact at $M$ precisely when the canonical map from the image of the incoming arrow (the kernel of its cokernel) to the kernel of the outgoing arrow is an isomorphism. The equivalences preserve these objects and this map, and reflect its invertibility. Hence the functor comparisons of Steps 2–5 transport exact sequences and exactness of the operations. Finally Step 7 expresses the internal base-change map, after applying an equivalence, as the sectionwise map conjugated by natural isomorphisms. If the latter is invertible, that composite is invertible, and applying the quasi-inverse shows the internal map invertible. This includes empty opens, the identity open, zero modules, and the zero coefficient ring without any extra hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), equivalences preserve limits and colimits; kernel/cokernel exactness and the inverse-conjugation calculation are written out here.
